plotSections.title: Preparing to Confront the Helm
bullets: After dinner at the table, Walker prepares to attempt contact with the helm again; Sylan asks if he needs magical fortitude, noting he has something that can stop a possession.

Walker says his last attempt was a pleasant conversation with Garrick, though not the Garrick the party knows now; he believes the person they first fought was truly Garrick and not someone possessed by the helm, which Sylan supports since that foe cast spells.
Walker decides to go ahead without much help, with Sylan patting him on the shoulder for luck.

plotSections.title: Phylactery Search
bullets: Before risking possession, Walker suggests testing suspicious items with the Soul identifier bag, which reveals whether an object is a phylactery (it burns/smolders if so).
The eagle troop marker (Hunched eagle marker) was tested: no smoldering or burning, so it is not a phylactery.
Ord lists a Helix medallion and an origami beetle taken from someone's desk; the party suspects the beetle may hold a message and Ord begins inspecting it.

Sylan mentions a fancy gold bar and a broken longsword from a crashed skyship in a swamp; the party debates how small or mundane a phylactery could be (coins, a grain of sand), noting it is usually an object important to the mage before becoming a lich.

chronologicalEvents: Dinner ends; the party sits at the table as the candles burn down.
Sylan offers Walker magical fortitude against possession before he uses the helm.
Walker recounts his previous pleasant conversation with Garrick through the helm and believes the first foe fought was Garrick himself.
Walker decides to proceed without extra protection.
Walker proposes testing suspicious items in the Soul identifier before possibly getting possessed.
The eagle troop marker is placed in the Soul identifier and shows no reaction.
Ord produces a Helix medallion and an origami beetle from someone's desk; he starts inspecting the beetle for a message.
The party discusses what objects could be phylacteries.
